etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: The adjective is first attested in 1531, the verb in 1551; borrowed from Latin articulātus (“distinct, articulated, jointed”), perfect passive participle of articulō, see -ate (etymology 1, 2 and 3). Regular participial usage of the adjective up until Early Modern English.
senses: Speaking in a clear and effective manner; having both good articulation and good elocution.
(zoology) An animal of the subkingdom Articulata.
